title: Structural and practical identifiability analysis of partially observed dynamical models by exploiting the profile likelihood

content.abstract_summary: Introduces the profile likelihood approach to simultaneously detect structural non-identifiabilities (functionally related parameter combinations that produce identical model outputs regardless of data quality) and practical non-identifiabilities (arising from finite, noisy data) in partially observed dynamical models described by ODEs. Derives confidence intervals from the profile. Foundational methods paper for identifiability analysis in biological dynamical systems — widely cited as the standard methodology for practical identifiability in systems biology and pharmacometrics.
key_findings: Profile likelihood approach distinguishes two distinct causes of non-identifiability: (1) structural — parameters are functionally related and cannot be separated even with infinite perfect data; (2) practical — parameters are theoretically identifiable but not from the available finite noisy data
Confidence intervals for parameters can be derived directly from the profile likelihood — superior to asymptotic (Fisher information matrix-based) intervals which assume local quadratic approximation
Structural non-identifiabilities manifest as flat profile likelihood ridges in the parameter space — detectable even without knowing the analytical parameter relationships
Method applies to partially observed systems (not all states measured) — the typical situation in clinical pharmacology and pharmacokinetics
Implementation: PottersWheel modeling toolbox for MATLAB; open source. The method has since been implemented in many pharmacometrics tools
limitations: Profile likelihood is computationally expensive for high-dimensional parameter spaces — scales poorly beyond ~20 parameters without approximation
Requires optimization from multiple starting points to avoid local minima being misidentified as global profiles

Does not address identifiability of neural network components or ML-augmented ODE systems — extending profile likelihood to neural ODE hybrid models is an open problem (directly addressed by campo_manzanares_2026)

extracted_claims.text: "We suggest an approach that exploits the profile likelihood. It enables to detect structural non-identifiabilities, which manifest in functionally related model parameters. Furthermore, practical non-identifiabilities are detected, that might arise due to limited amount and quality of experimental data."

gaps_addressed: Provides the methodological foundation for M1.2 and M1.3 — any WG analysis of identifiability of neural ODE components must establish what profile likelihood says about the mechanistic parameters first, before extending to the ML components

The structural/practical identifiability distinction is the key conceptual frame for M1.2 — neural ODE components are generally structurally non-identifiable (redundant weight configurations), which is a different type of non-identifiability than the parameter correlations Raue addresses
Defines confidence intervals from profile likelihood — the gold standard that campo_manzanares_2026's MQRI is trying to match with FIM-based approximations for neural architectures

provenance.notes: Found via targeted PMID lookup (PMID 19505944). Bioinformatics 2009, 25(15):1923-1929. University of Freiburg Physics Institute group (Timmer lab). This is the most-cited identifiability methods paper in systems biology and is the standard reference for practical identifiability in pharmacometrics contexts. Abstract only but content is well-known; detailed methods are described in the abstract and widely reproduced. Upgrade to full_text not required for WG purposes — use as foundational reference in M1.2 literature review.
